assessment: The incumbent plausibly handles stable courses adequately: unchanged-assignment centers had seven-minute median handling, versus 17 overall. Its sampled course-set accuracy was 80%, below the 95% target. Assignment changes accompany six affected exports, supporting investigation of current-assignment selection without establishing causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation: apparent absence could involve naming or comparison. Replacement delivery greatly exceeds execution time, but elapsed waiting is not measured active handling. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course center.

openings.claim: Selecting courses using current instructor assignments may misrepresent requested-week membership; stable course identifiers plus week-effective membership could reduce these errors.
openings.delta: Test historical inclusion semantics behind the existing CSV export while independently testing whether renames merely disguise present courses.
openings.prediction: With names held fixed, changing only the current assignment changes incumbent inclusion for an identical requested week; week-effective selection removes that dependence. A rename-only discrepancy may persist in coordinator recognition despite correct membership.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, replay fixed-week cases varying assignment and name separately, plus a split-course case across center boundaries. Compare exported course membership with explicit fixture expectations, check CSV compatibility and continue attendance writes. Estimate history availability, engineer effort and hosting cost before choosing a bounded implementation.
assumptions: Week-effective membership can be established reliably.
A correction can fit six engineer-days and existing hosting without blocking attendance entry.

openings.claim: Does reconciling course identity consume most active handling, or does substantial work remain when the course set is already verified?
openings.delta: Separates export-selection improvements from downstream spreadsheet work that current logs cannot reveal.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, prior course-set verification sharply reduces checking time; if importing dominates, verified files retain substantial handling time.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions for counterbalanced fabricated tasks with matched documented-schema files, one with an independently verified course mapping. Time checking, correction, downloading and importing separately; record replacement waiting separately from active work. Keep sessions inside authorized workspaces and cap engineering support within six days.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary spreadsheet work.
Independent verification reflects each coordinator's intended course set.
